source_text.body:
Build a website and backend with Copilot agent mode
A commenter used Copilot to create their website, finding it especially good at API and backend server setup, using agent mode and instruction files.
·
Nov 18, 2026
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
What they did
A commenter said they used Copilot with a BYOK DeepSeek API key, selecting the Pro mode, to build their website. They describe it as especially strong for API and backend server setup and creation, while using Luna and Auto for iOS app work; the thread also mentions instruction files and agent mode more generally, but this commenter did not say those were part of their own setup.
How it went
They said the DeepSeek plus Copilot mix worked well for a React website with a database and APIs. The only concrete limit they gave was plan usage: on Pro+ they were already at 90.3% after several hours a day of coding.
Worth knowing
The practical catch was cost and credits: they recommend topping up a DeepSeek API key with about $10 and note that model choice heavily affects how fast Copilot credits run out.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
Using agent mode, build a [type of website, e.g. portfolio site] with a backend API for [main function, e.g. contact form and project listings]. First create an instructions file describing my stack ([framework, language, hosting]) and coding conventions, then set up the server routes and wire up the frontend. You're done when I can run it locally and the endpoints respond correctly. Show me the run commands at the end.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1xzhxdj/who_use_github_copilot_your_experience
